items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: That's Art Hodes, Walter Page is on bass, and Wild Bill Davidson.

ctx.x: Yeah, those were later. This is apparently 1947. Not apparently, it is 1947. I'll see if I can track it down for you.

Then, just while we're on Bechet, and you've done some work with Bechet... There's a quartet with Pops Foster and Lloyd Philips on Columbia, where you play "Buddy Bolden's Stomp" and "My Woman Blues." That was put out by Columbia. And then there's Bechet's Blue Note Jazzmen. That's Art Hodes, Walter Page is on bass, and Wild Bill Davidson. There's "Sister Kate," or I guess the full title is "I wish I Could Shimmy Like My Sister Kate" (these were for Blue Note), "Tiger Rag," "Tin Roof Blues," "I've Found A New…
Do you remember any of these recording sessions?
